entities.summary: Heinrich Carl von Schimmelmann was a German-born Danish merchant, banker and politician. He was the largest Danish slave owner and slave trader, owning over 1,000 slaves in his plantations in the Danish-owned West Indies. He became one of the absolute richest people in Denmark and, among other things, owned the Odd Fellow Palace. During the Seven Years' War, he speculated heavily on currency debasement in close association with his business partner Abel Seyler. After supporting Denmark–Norway as the head of the banking system in Denmark, he was rewarded by becoming a member of the Danish nobility.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Heinrich Carl von Schimmelmann's involvement in the slave trade and his ownership of over 1,000 slaves had significant regional impact on Denmark and its colonies in the Danish West Indies. His business practices also contributed to the country's economic instability during the Seven Years' War.
